article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Morning Brief
article.dek: Washington stole Thursday night late, the board still hasn't flipped, and Sunday's numbers go through Check.

items.headline: Lead: Washington steals Thursday night - Diggs with 57 seconds left, and the Giants let the division slip
paragraphs: Washington beat the Giants 24-21 on Thursday night at MetLife. Jayden Daniels found Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left, and Rasul Douglas intercepted J.J. McCarthy on the next drive to seal it.

The Giants had it. Isaiah Likely's 66-yard touchdown put them up 21-17 midway through the fourth, and they picked Daniels off twice after that - Jevon Holland and Ar'Darious Washington - but the offense could not get a first down on either possession. Washington went 71 yards in 49 seconds for the win.
Washington is 3-5-1 now and two back of the Giants in the loss column, with the tiebreaker in hand. The Giants are 5-3-1. Washington's next game is Monday night against the Bengals.
items.takeaway: Daniels to Diggs with 57 seconds left, Douglas seals it with an interception - Washington wins 24-21, takes the tiebreaker, and pulls within two of the Giants in the loss column.

items.headline: Injuries: nothing new since last night - Lock still throwing, Cross still back, designations land today
paragraphs: No new injury news overnight. The latest is still Thursday's practice report. Drew Lock was limited again with elbow and oblique injuries, but he resumed throwing, and he is still the starter with Sam Darnold ruled out. Darnold did not practice again with his ribs and quad injuries and is targeting a return in Week 12, after Seattle's bye.
Left tackle Charles Cross practiced for the first time since his Week 7 ankle injury, working as a limited participant. He has missed the last two games.

The Seahawks issue their final designations for Sunday's game in Las Vegas today, Friday. Inactives for every Sunday game come about 90 minutes before kickoff. One warning that has not changed: the app board still lists Darnold as Seattle's starter. Do not trust the board's quarterback names for Sunday.
items.takeaway: Lock resumed throwing and stays the starter with Darnold out until Week 12, Cross is back at practice for the first time since Week 7, and final designations land today - the board still lists Darnold as the starter.

items.headline: Sunday: thirteen games, an early kickoff, and the night games
paragraphs: No games today. Sunday has thirteen games. The early one is Patriots at Lions at 9:30 a.m. ET, then the main 1:00 p.m. ET window, and the night games are Steelers at Bengals at 8:20 p.m. ET on Sunday and Chargers at Ravens at 8:15 p.m. ET on Monday.

Two numbers to know before the board catches up: the Jaguars are the week's biggest favorite at -10.5 against the Titans, and the highest total on the board is 49ers at Cowboys at 55.5. Those are best-available prices across the books, not the app's numbers - the app board has not flipped yet, so run any price you like through Check.
items.takeaway: Thirteen games Sunday, starting with Patriots at Lions at 9:30 a.m. ET - the Jaguars are the biggest favorite at -10.5 and 49ers at Cowboys carries the week's highest total at 55.5.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The board still has not flipped - Sunday still goes through Check
paragraphs: I checked the board after the morning refresh. It is the same board as yesterday - generated November 2, still showing Week 8, now eleven days old. The only game with a market board is Bears at Seahawks, played November 2.

So the headline cards are still from a finished game, and they must not be bet. For the record, they read: Hit Rate on the Seahawks moneyline at -175, Balanced and Value both on the Bears +3 at -102. Those games are done. Do not bet those cards.

Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win. Balanced is the strong pick without paying too much. Value is always the model's +EV play. Hit Rate is not worse for not being +EV. It is a different job: most likely to win.

Until the board flips, Sunday has no card at all. That is what Check is for. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: The board is still the November 2 board, eleven days old, still showing Week 8 - it still lists Darnold as Seattle's starter and knows nothing about Sunday - so Sunday's prices go through Check.

items.headline: Learn the Game: the vig - the price of placing the bet
paragraphs: The vig - short for vigorish, also called the juice - is the book's cut, built into the price. It is why a standard bet is -110 instead of even money.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: you bet $1.10 to win $1.00 at -110. If you win, you get your $1.10 back plus $1.00. If you lose, the book keeps your $1.10. The extra 10 cents is the vig.

That is why a -110 bet has to win about 52.4% of the time just to break even. The vig is the reason shopping for a better price - -105 instead of -110, or +100 instead of -110 - is real money over a season. Run the better price through Check before you bet it.
items.takeaway: The vig is the book's cut built into the price - at -110 you risk $1.10 to win $1.00, so a bet has to win about 52.4% of the time to break even, which is why a better price is real money.

items.headline: The total fell four points and still went over - and the favorite lost outright
paragraphs: The total kept sliding all week. It opened at 44.5, was 41.5 on Wednesday evening, and closed at 40.5 at DraftKings. The final score was 24-21 - 45 points. The over cashed anyway.

The spread did not move: the Giants closed -2.5, moneyline -142, with Washington +120. Washington won outright. The public and the money agreed on the Giants - more than three-quarters of the bets, per VSiN, as the line moved from -1.5 to -2.5 - and tickets and handle on the same side is not a Fade. Nothing in the market argued against the move. The move lost anyway.

The lesson is not that the market was wrong. It is that a falling total is not a prediction, and a favorite is not a result. When the board flips, Sunday's totals go through the same check: the app's number, your book's price, and Check for the verdict.
items.takeaway: The total fell from 44.5 to 40.5 and still went over at 45 points, the Giants closed -2.5 and lost outright - the public and the money agreed on the favorite, and the move lost anyway.

items.headline: Friday's job: designations first, then your number before the rush
paragraphs: Final designations land this afternoon. That is the one thing worth waiting for today - if a player you need is questionable, wait for the designation, then decide. Inactives come about 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday.

Everything else, do now. If your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet it now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number on Sunday, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too - and the Sunday late rush on big-name teams pushes lines past the app's playable number.

And a word on the tracker, because it only works if you are honest with yourself: settlement is manual, there is no auto-settle. Log the losers too. A tracker that only holds winners is a story, not a record.
items.takeaway: Final designations land today - that is the one thing worth waiting for - then if your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet it now, and log the losers too, because the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself.
